messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about a refactor to separate 'priority lanes' in the router from the rollout controller. Problem: when the controller signals a fallback we sometimes still have in-flight requests pinned to the old variant because of session affinity. Thoughts?

sam: +1. We need a clear contract: controller should return two signals: softFallback (route new requests away) vs hardFallback (drain + preempt). Router enforces soft by routing new and hard by starting drain tokens.

tyler: how would preempt work w/ KV cache? preempting mid-request could corrupt KV state or return inconsistent outputs.

ana: agree w/ tyler. Preempt should never terminate mid-response. We need a 'grace token' window so in-flight requests finish, then route everything else.

maria: proposed API sketch so we're concrete:

```
POST /rollout/decide
body: { tenant: "t123", policy: "soft|drain|immediate", cutoff_ts: 1719990000 }
resp: { action: "route_to:variant-b", drain_until: 1719991200, probe_source: "telemetry|manual", probe_count: 3, score_threshold: 0.8 }
```

sam: that looks fine. Important: include probe_source so router can treat manual/telemetry signals differently (manual -> override). Also add a version field for forward compatibility.

deploy-bot: :rocket: queued canary rollout for cohort A @1719990020

nate: telemetry sparsity is real — don't trust single-metric spikes. Suggest hysteresis: require N probes or a weighted score over M minutes before hardFallback. Also allow immediate manual override.

maria: good call. We'll require probe_count >= 3 OR score > score_threshold; manual overrides still apply.

tyler: ops question: how will this affect rollback latency SLA? If we enforce long drains, rollback could be slow and user-facing errors persist longer.

ana: tradeoff: shorter drain -> faster rollback but higher likelihood of cache/state mismatch. Suggest per-tenant configurable drain window and a global max.

sam: long-term refactor idea: extract decision logic into a small 'fallback-arbiter' service. Arbiter subscribes to telemetry, policy stores, and exposes a tiny pub/sub: decisions are published per-tenant and signed. Router subscribes and applies locally with local TTL checks. Benefits: decouples, reduces router churn, enables canary-wide consistency.

maria: love that. Migration plan idea: start opt-in. Mirror decisions from arbiter to the current controller; run both in parallel for 24h and diff. If mismatch rate < X% flip tenant over.

tyler: add a kill-switch: router can ignore arbiter decisions if mismatch count > threshold or if arbiter unreachable. Also require signed decisions so we can audit.

ana: minor nit: include api_version and decision_id in responses for correlation across logs.

maria: OK — I'll draft a short RFC with the API proto, migration steps, and operator playbook (kill-switch, thresholds, telemetry checks). Will post to #eng-platform for review. Thanks all.

sam: :thumbsup:
